result: `/output/lib/pyint.mjs` exports `PyValueError` (an `Error` subclass with `name = 'PyValueError'` and `pyType = 'ValueError'`), `pyStrip(s)`, `isPyDecimalDigit(cp)`, `pyDigitValue(cp)`, and `pyInt(s)`; it imports `pyRepr` from `./pyrepr.mjs` for the error message and is pure ESM with zero dependencies. `pyStrip` uses an explicit frozen set of CPython `str.isspace()` code points — I included U+001C–U+001F and U+0085 (NEL) in addition to the ones the spec enumerated, since CPython strips those too, and deliberately excluded U+200B and U+FEFF so `'3\u200b'` raises. `isPyDecimalDigit` tests `/\p{Nd}/u` against `String.fromCodePoint(cp)` (guarding out-of-range/non-integer inputs) and `pyDigitValue` finds the block zero by walking back at most 9 steps while the predecessor is still Nd; both memoize into module-level `Map`s. `pyInt` strips, iterates by code point via `[...s]` (so astral digits like U+1D7CE work), accepts only an ASCII `+`/`-` sign (U+2212 rejected), requires at least one digit, permits `_` only as a single separator between digits (tracked with a `prevWasUnderscore` flag that also catches the trailing-underscore case), accumulates with `v = v * 10n + BigInt(d)`, and returns `0n` early when the magnitude is zero so `'-0'` normalizes. Judgement calls: on any failure it throws with the *original unstripped* string passed to `pyRepr`; a non-string argument also raises `PyValueError` rather than a TypeError (the caller only ever passes strings, so this is a defensive path); and `pyDigitValue` returns `-1` for non-Nd code points instead of throwing, letting `pyInt` own all error construction. I verified against a stub `pyrepr.mjs` in a temp dir (since the real one did not yet exist), then re-verified against the real module once it appeared — all accept/reject cases from the spec pass, including the big-integer, Arabic-Indic, Devanagari, and fullwidth cases; no files other than the requested one were created under `/output`.

/output/lib/iterutils.mjs exports three names: `pyBool(x)` (Python truthiness — false only for `false`/`null`/`undefined`/numeric zero/`0n`/`''`/empty array/empty `Map`/empty `Set`, and deliberately **true** for `NaN` since Python's `float('nan')` is truthy), `partition(src, key = pyBool)` returning `new PyTuple([trues, falses])` with original relative order preserved in each list, and `bucketize(src, key = pyBool, { valueTransform = null, keyFilter = null } = {})` returning a `Map` whose keys land in first-occurrence order with original element order inside each bucket. Both accept any iterable (arrays, strings, `Set`, generators), consume it once via `for...of`, and never mutate it; `src` without `Symbol.iterator` raises `TypeError: expected an iterable src, not …`, and a `key` that is neither callable nor a string raises `TypeError: expected callable or string, not …` (non-callable `valueTransform`/`keyFilter` raise the analogous boltons messages). Judgement calls: (1) real boltons implements `partition` as `bucketize(src, key).get(True/False)`, which only works because Python hashes `True == 1`; a JS `Map` does not, so `partition` applies the truthiness test (`pyBool` of the key result) directly and always returns exactly two lists, while `bucketize` keeps the raw key value as the `Map` key without coercion, matching boltons for arbitrary key functions. (2) The string-key form mirrors boltons' `getattr(x, key, x)` — it falls back to the element itself when the property is absent (`null`/`undefined` elements pass through). (3) Because `pyrepr.mjs` did not yet exist when I wrote the file, `makePyTuple` tolerates either plausible `PyTuple` shape (plain wrapper vs. `Array` subclass, where the inherited single-argument constructor would nest the pair); the sibling module landed as the wrapper form (`class PyTuple { constructor(items) }`), and I verified end-to-end with the real `/output/lib/pyrepr.mjs` and `/output/lib/pyint.mjs` that all ten spec input cases reproduce the reference stdout verbatim. No other files were created.

Created `/output/lib/pyrepr.mjs` (the only file I wrote; `iterutils.mjs` and `pyint.mjs` there are from sibling agents). It exports `pyIsPrintable(cp)`, `pyRepr(value)`, `pyStr(value)`, `pyPrint(value)`, and `class PyTuple` (with `items`, a `length` getter, and `Symbol.iterator`). Judgement calls: (1) printability is implemented as the single positive rule `PRINTABLE = /^[\p{L}\p{M}\p{N}\p{P}\p{S}]$/u.test(chr) || cp === 0x20`, with a 256-entry memo cache for the Latin-1 hot path and `false` returned for out-of-range/non-integer inputs; I verified it against CPython's `str.isprintable()` for all 1,114,112 code points — 0 disagreements in the Python-printable-but-mine-not direction and 627 in the other direction, all of which are code points assigned in Unicode 15.1+ that Node's ICU knows but the local Python's unicodedata 15.0 does not (e.g. U+2FFC–U+2FFF, CJK Ext I at U+2EBF0+), i.e. a data-version artifact, not a logic gap, and irrelevant to every spec case. (2) String repr iterates by code point via `for...of`, applies escapes in the mandated order (backslash, active quote, `\n`/`\r`/`\t`, then `\xNN`/`\uNNNN`/`\UNNNNNNNN` in lowercase zero-padded hex), and picks `"` only when the string has a `'` and no `"`; I fuzz-checked it against Python `repr()` on 4001 strings drawn from a tricky code-point pool (quotes, backslash, C0/C1, NBSP, U+200B, U+2028/9, U+2212, lone-surrogate-free astral, unassigned U+0378) with 0 mismatches, and lone surrogates fall through to `\udNNN` as CPython does. (3) `undefined` is treated as `None` alongside `null` for defensiveness; plain Numbers render integrally without `.0` when `Number.isInteger` (normalizing `-0` to `0`) and otherwise via `String(n)`, with `nan`/`inf`/`-inf` special-cased — this path is not used by the program's BigInt-based ints. (4) `pyStr` returns a top-level string raw and delegates everything else to `pyRepr`, so container elements always use repr; `Map` iterates in insertion order so bucketize key order is preserved, and `PyTuple` emits `()`, `(a,)`, `(a, b)`.

Created `/output/lib/argparse.mjs` (only that file; the sibling `iterutils.mjs`/`pyint.mjs`/`pyrepr.mjs` were pre-existing and untouched), exporting exactly two symbols: `basename(p)` (pure-JS, last non-empty '/'-segment, `'/'`→`''`) and `class ArgumentParser` with `add_argument(...flags, {type, required, help, action, dest, metavar, default, const})`, `parse_args(argv)`, `parse_known_args(argv)`, `format_usage()`, `format_help()`, `print_usage(write)`, `print_help(write)`, `error(message)` and `exit(status, message)`; internally it is a direct port of CPython 3.12's `_parse_known_args` / `_parse_optional` / `_get_option_tuples` / `_match_argument` / `_get_nargs_pattern` plus `HelpFormatter._format_usage` and `_format_action`, so `--` handling, prefix-abbreviation with ambiguity errors, `--opt=value`, bundled short options, required-before-unrecognized ordering, error wording, stderr routing and exit codes (0 for `--help`, 2 for errors) are reproduced exactly. Judgement calls worth flagging: (1) the negative-number matcher uses `/^-\p{Nd}+\n?$|^-\p{Nd}*\.\p{Nd}+\n?$/u` rather than a literal `\d` translation, because Python's `\d` is Unicode-aware (`--a -٣` is accepted as a value, verified against the reference) and Python's `$` also matches before one trailing newline; (2) terminal width is hard-coded to 80 columns (CPython's non-TTY fallback) instead of reading `COLUMNS`, so help layout is deterministic; (3) the built-in `-h/--help` action uses an internal `SUPPRESS` dest so `help` does not appear on the returned namespace, matching `vars(args)`; (4) argparse's own tiny diagnostics (`ignored explicit argument 'x'`, `invalid <type> value: 'x'`) use a local minimal quoting helper rather than importing `pyrepr.mjs`, to keep the module import-free as required; (5) positionals, subparsers, nargs, choices and mutually-exclusive groups are deliberately unimplemented and documented as such, though `consume_positionals` is retained as an identity function so the surrounding control flow — and hence the `unrecognized arguments: --` behavior — stays faithful.
